steps.message:
Item 048 on our Package A register falls due on 07/20/2026, and the Block B plant-room excavation the Contractor has planned for 08/10/2026 cannot start until it is closed. I am taking it myself. Item 048 is the Kesterline shoring design for that excavation. Kesterline has since supplemented the sealed Rev.1 with Rev.2, sent under its letter KE-L-2026-0713, which is attached, and is asking for verification on that basis so that the excavation can go ahead. Verify the item on its current revision against the logged groundwater and subsurface conditions.

Work it through against the project record and issue the verification memo, addressed to Rachel Marlbeck, on the attached memorandum form, keeping its sections. Set out the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition; say which of the design's checks can be carried forward as they stand and which, if any, cannot; say what the excavation this item releases would do to the permanent work already built at Block B; say what has to be produced before the excavation can start and who has to produce it; and say what the disposition means for the 08/10/2026 excavation start. Give the register response you would record under my name, A. Vance, dated 07/20/2026, and the status the item should carry, closing it only if you have verified it. Save the memo as /filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item048_BlockB.docx.

7.  GROUNDWATER CONDITIONS
7.1  Design Water Table — Upper Sand
Groundwater within the upper SP-SM sand is unconfined, hosted between the top of the clay at El. 738.0 (as its
lower boundary) and a phreatic surface at approximately El. 742.0. Piezometer readings from the three shallow
standpipes (B-01, B-03, B-09) taken during the 11/2024 through 02/2025 monitoring period range from
El. 741.6 to El. 742.4, essentially stable across the record. Groundwater seepage was observed during
exploratory test-pit excavation in the Block A area at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2.
The design water table for the Package A project is set at El. 742.0. This elevation is to be used by the
Structural Engineer of Record and the Architect of Record for hydrostatic uplift on the basement mat, for
hydrostatic head on the below-grade waterproofing system and for design of the temporary sheeting and
dewatering system during construction. Because the design water table is stable across a full year of monitoring
and is consistent with regional experience, no seasonal adjustment or design margin is added above El. 742.0
for this project.
7.2  Confined Piezometric Head — Deep Aquifer
Groundwater within the deep SW-GW sand and gravel aquifer is confined by the CL clay aquitard. Piezometric
head measured in the two deep piezometers (screened below El. 720.0 in Borings B-04 and B-08) is at El. 738.0
— essentially at the top of the clay, or about 18 ft above the top of the aquifer itself. Individual readings range
from El. 737.7 to El. 738.3 across the monitoring period, with no discernible trend and no seasonal variation
exceeding a few tenths of a foot.
The physical interpretation is that the deep aquifer is recharged upstream of the site at a higher elevation and
discharges downstream through the same continuous outwash body; the clay acts as an aquitard that prevents
equalization of the two heads. The confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 is the elevation to which water will
rise in any well, boring or excavation that penetrates the clay and exposes the underlying aquifer. Any
excavation that either (a) penetrates the clay and enters the aquifer, or (b) reduces the effective weight of the
clay plug between the excavation subgrade and the top of the aquifer, will be subject to upward hydrostatic
pressure equal to the confined head above the point in question.
